1.why: 252 = 42 x 6 exactly, the only product relation in the set (item null 0.00); betting the directional rule that the key IS the product.

2.why: 8 is the derivational hub - 8^2 = 64, 8/4 = 2, 8 x 1.5 = 12 - and every other option is generated from it.

3.why: 68, 8, 15, 4 share no arithmetic, geometric, hub or product relation; nothing distinguishes them.

4.why: 47 + 43 = 90 fires the angle-pair rule but that channel is at its noise floor here and does not say which member of the pair is the key.

5.why: 2x4 and 4x2 form a transpose pair, which narrows the key to those two, but the set is not a complete closed set and nothing breaks the tie.

6.why: 80 is the middle of the arithmetic run 40, 80, 120, but the arithmetic-middle channel ran at 4 observed against 1.4-2.6 expected, i.e. noise.

7.why: 1, i, -1, -i is the complete closed set of powers of i - every option is equally legal and the closure gives a solver nothing.

8.why: 5 is the middle of the geometric run 1, 5, 25 with 13 as the lone outlier.

9.why: 42 is the middle of the doubling run 21, 42, 84 with 56 the outlier; the competing hub flag on 84 rests only on the 84->56 = 2/3 leg and is a detector artefact.

10.why: 62 is the middle of 50, 62, 74 but that channel is at noise and 99 is an unremarkable outlier.

11.why: -7, -5, 0, 17 fire no channel; the lone zero is a form outlier whose direction is a coin flip.

12.why: 60 is simultaneously the geometric middle of 36, 60, 100 (ratio 5/3) and the arithmetic middle of 20, 60, 100 - two channels converge on one option.

13.why: 24 + 336 = 360 fires the angle rule at noise level and does not pick between them; 512 being the lone power of two is directionless.

14.why: 147 is a magnitude outlier among 18, 19, 21 but outlier direction is a coin flip and no relation is exact.

15.why: 19.5 and 13.5 are the decimals and 39 = 2 x 19.5, but form-outlier direction is unbettable and the doubling does not reach the middle-of-run channel.

16.why: 18:24 and 48:64 are both 3:4 and 24, 48 doubles, but no three options form a single run so no channel fires.

17.why: 7, 35, 12, -2 show only 7 x 5 = 35, which is not a within-set product relation; nothing decides.

18.why: 72 + 18 = 90 fires the angle-pair rule at noise level and cannot choose between the two members.

19.why: 10 = -5 x -2 fires the product rule, but sum (5) and difference (10, -5) fire on the same tiny closely-spaced set, so the product hit is not separable from noise here.

20.why: 66 is the lone non-power-of-two, which eliminates it as an added-instead-of-multiplied trap but leaves 128, 32, 256 undecided.

21.why: 4, 39, 12, 44 fire nothing; 4 and 12 share a factor but that relation reaches no option set channel.

22.why: 5/3 and 3/5 are a reciprocal pair and 24 is the magnitude outlier, but reciprocal-pair direction is a coin flip.

23.why: 1 + 3i is the derivational hub: 1 - 3i is its conjugate, 2 + 6i is twice it, and 3 + i is its components swapped - all three distractors are generated from it.

24.why: 15 is a near-hub (15^2 = 225, 15 x 3 = 45) but the 8 leg fails, so it misses the channel that was actually measured above null.

25.why: 18 is both the geometric middle of 6, 18, 54 and the full derivational hub (x1.5 = 27, /3 = 6, x3 = 54) - the two live channels agree.

26.why: 5, 33, 27, 25 fire no channel; 25 = 5^2 and 27 = 3^3 are unrelated to each other.

27.why: 96 x 2 = 192 and 16 x 6 = 96 but no three options form a geometric run and no option is a hub over all three others.

28.why: -5 and 5 are a sign pair, which is a form outlier with no bettable direction; 24 and 11 are unrelated.
